AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on
a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have any question
about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Library, Arts and Culture
Department, at (818) 548-2030, during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  MAY 19, 2022 AT 2:00 PM

  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS

8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, May 19, 2022 at 2:00 p.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on May 19, 2022 at 2:11 p.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  •  The Agenda for the May 19, 2022 Regular Meeting was posted on May 11, 2022 on the Bulletin
  Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the March 10, 2022 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.
  b. Minutes of the March 17, 2022 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.
  c. Minutes of the March 22, 2022 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.
  d. Minutes of the March 31, 2022 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.
  e. Minutes of the April 7, 2022 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal Arts & Culture
  Administrator

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes. Members of
  the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the Speaker, but there will be no Debate or
  Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  - No Speakers

 5. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. City of Glendale Code of Conduct for Councilmembers and Members of Boards and
  Commissions.
  1. Motion to Note and File the City of Glendale Code of Conduct for Councilmembers and Members of
  Boards and Commissions.

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  1
   That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby receives, notes, and files the “City of Glendale Code
  of Conduct for Councilmembers and Members of Boards and Commissions,” approved by the City
  Council on August 24, 2021, as more fully outlined in the May 19, 2022 Report by the Library, Arts
  & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  b. Brand 50 Arts Programming and Sponsorship Opportunity
  1. Motion to approve (1) the funding of a proposal by the Brand Associates to provide arts
  programming associated with Brand 50, and (2) the sponsorship of the Brand 50 Annual National
  Juried Exhibition of Works on Paper in an amount not to exceed $2,500 from the 2021-2022 Work
  Plan.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Tufenkian

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves (1) the funding of a proposal by the Brand
  Associates to provide arts programming associated with Brand 50, and (2) the sponsorship of the
  Brand 50 Annual National Juried Exhibition of Works on Paper in an amount not to exceed $2,500
  from the 2021-2022 Work Plan, as more fully outlined in the May 19, 2022 Report by the Library,
  Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

6. DISCUSSION ITEM(s) / REPORT(s)
  a. Artsakh Creative Program – Update

  •  Juan Gonzalez, Neighborhood Services Supervisor, shared a presentation on the Artsakh
  Creative Retail Pop Up Pilot Program, and introduced the current participants of the
  program.

  c. Arts and Culture Commission Website – City-Wide Arts Calendar
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a brief overview of Sydney Brundige, who began working
  with the Arts and Culture Commission through the Federal Work-study provided by
  Claremont Graduate University. Ms. Brundige’s first project directive was to review the
  Arts Calendar on the Arts and Culture Commission’s website
  (www.glendaleartsandculture.org).
  • Ms. Sydney Brundige made a presentation on the Arts Calendar updates.

  c. 2021-2022 Work Plan Progress Updates

  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that Staff is working with the Museum of Neon Art (MONA) to
  confirm their plans for their “Glendale Electric!” event set for June 11, 2022 from 12:00 PM
  – 5:00PM at various locations in Glendale. Staff is also working with Cathy Hrenda to
  install her sculpture, “Ride Like the Wind,” to be located in the Drought Tolerant Garden in
  2
   front of Central Library. As of May 19, 2022, 15 out of 17 Art Happens Anywhere (AHA)
  projects will have been successfully launched.

  ii. LeBasse Projects – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that the Commission hosted a Special Meeting on April 7, 2022
  to review design concept proposals for the Glenoaks Blvd. Median Sculpture.

  iii. Mural Ordinance – Update

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that Staff is working with Ms. Odenkirk on drafting a Mural
  Ordinance in addition to Policies and Procedures which will complement the Mural
  Ordinance.

  iv. Creative Crosswalks

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that Staff is working with Public Works staff who are
  assessing the possibility of incorporating a larger palette of colors for the Creative
  Crosswalks RFP.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – Update
  i. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station – Exhibits Update

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that Staff met with the Artist Review & Selection
  Committee for the Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station Exhibits. Staff received a total
  of 14 applications for consideration, and Commissioners Tufenkian and Zadorian
  reviewed the recommendations and provided their feedback. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave
  a brief overview of the artists and art selected.

  3. PERFORMING ARTS – No Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update

  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS
  i. Public Relations Firm – RFP Update

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that Staff is working on a draft Public Relations Firm – RFP
  with the intention of hiring a public relations firm to strategically perform communication,
  marketing, branding, and public relations services for City-sponsored arts and cultural
  events, exhibits and public art.

7. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  •  Commissioner Tufenkian recommended that an Armenian artist be used to provide the art in front of
  the Armenian Museum that is currently under construction; Commissioner Zadorian suggested
  waiting on discussion within the Commission about an artist being used to install an art piece at the
  Armenian Museum. Dr. Shaffer stated that discussion with Museum representatives is currently
  underway.
  •  Commissioner Vidor stated she is excited and happy about all the programming within Glendale.
  She thanked both Ms. Fukutomi-Jones and Dr. Shaffer. The Commission thanked both Ms.
  Fukutomi-Jones and Dr. Shaffer.
  •  Dr. Shaffer stated that the Glendale Library, Arts & Culture has been selected by the Institute of
  Museum and Library Services as one of finalists for the National Medal.

  3
 8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - None

9. ADJOURNMENT: 4:08 p.m.
The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is June 16, 2022, at 2:00 p.m., in City Council
Chambers (2nd Floor), 613 E. Broadway.
